statement: When a report value collapses two states the renderer cannot tell apart, write copy true of both instead of asserting either. Cejel records coverage_percent as 0 both when no coverage report or threshold states a percentage and when one states exactly 0, so the 0.6.0 certificate's '0/100 percent' read to a diligence reader as 'express has 0% coverage'. The fix says 'no published coverage percentage above 0' and states how the rubric scores it (0 of 100). It stays presentation-only, because a report field to separate the states would move every pinned report hash. Rule: before rendering a number, ask which states produce it; if they differ in meaning and the artifact cannot distinguish them, word the line so it is true for every one and say what the score does with it.

Two counts of the same population on one artifact must share a denominator or name the difference. The certificate's summary box counted every criterion ('code 2/5 · process 3/6 measured · low confidence'), 'What was established' counted only applicable ones ('5 of 5'), and the low-confidence flag silently counted not-applicable dimensions as unmeasured, so a first-time reader could not reconcile them. Each statement was correct alone; together they read as a contradiction. Rule: before adding or changing a count on a reader surface, find every other count of the same thing on that surface and make them visibly add up, naming any remainder (here, '6 do not apply').
